findings.title: Wire graph still lists ProvideAnonDBStore, which now needs an int64 and has no consumer
findings.body: `pkg/server/wire.go:374-375` still registers `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds `anonstore.AnonStore` to it. The function now takes `deviceLimit int64` (line 52), and no wire provider supplies an `int64`. `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now builds the store itself (`impl.go:43`), and the only other consumer is `api.NewAnonDeviceServiceAPI`, which is called by hand. So nothing in the graph consumes `AnonStore` any more. Wire rejects both an unused provider and an unsatisfied `int64` input. `wire_gen.go` is not checked in, so code generation for the server injector will fail and the binary will not build. Remove `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and its `wire.Bind` from `pkg/server/wire.go`.

findings.title: A rejected device is cached, so its next request gets in and the limit does nothing
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device key to `localCache` (line 87) before it calls `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (line 93), and it does not remove the key on error. Take a new device that arrives once the limit is reached: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` rejects that one request (`client.go:45-46`). For the next 29 minutes, every other request from that device on the same instance hits the cache at lines 83-84. `TagDevice` then returns nil and the device is authenticated anonymously. A page load sends many parallel requests, so in practice only the first one fails. The device never gets a DB row, so it is not counted either, and any number of devices over the limit can use the instance. Fix: only set the cache entry after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or delete the key when it returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, so concurrent new devices can go over the limit
findings.body: The `CountDevices` check (line 110) and the insert (lines 149-153) run in separate sessions with no lock. With N instances, or concurrent first requests from different devices, all of them can read `count < limit` and insert. If the limit is a soft cap this is acceptable, but consider documenting that. If it must be a hard cap, use one conditional statement or a transaction.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from a background goroutine onto the request path for every deployment
findings.body: Before this change, `TagDevice` ran in a goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout. Now it runs synchronously inside `Authenticate` with the request context, even when `device_limit` is 0. Each uncached anonymous request now waits for the upsert. When a limit is set, it also waits for a `COUNT(*)` over `anon_device` (`database.go:110`). A request cancelled by the client now also cancels the tag write. To keep the old latency for the default configuration, you could tag synchronously only when `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0`.

findings.title: Limit test does not check that a known device can still be updated at the limit
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only checks that a second, new device is rejected. The `updateDevice` path, which lets an existing device refresh while the limit is reached, has no test. Neither does the auth-level behaviour, where `Authenticate` returns an error and a repeat request should still be rejected; that missing test would have caught the cache bypass in `impl.go`. The second device is also named `"keep"` even though it is the one being rejected, which is misleading.

findings.title: New `device_limit` setting is not in defaults.ini or the docs
findings.body: `device_limit` is read from `[auth.anonymous]`, but a repository search finds no other mention of it, in `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini` or the docs. Operators cannot find the setting, and nothing tells them what happens at the limit: new anonymous devices are rejected and existing ones keep working for 30 days after their last activity.

findings.title: Field type is inferred as `undefined`, while the backend always sends a number
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` with no annotation makes the class field's type `undefined`, so `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` cannot be used as a number without a cast. The backend DTO is a plain `int64` (`frontend_settings.go:195`), so the value is `0` when no limit is set, never `undefined`. Consider `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`, or typing it as `number` with default `0`. Nothing in the frontend reads this field yet.

contracts.action: Anonymous authentication now tags the device synchronously and fails auth with ErrDeviceLimitReached
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous async goroutine tagging in the same function, and tagDeviceUI's local cache
contracts.before_after: tagDeviceUI sets the cache key before the DB write and never clears it on error, so only the first request per device per 29 min reaches the limit check
contracts.visible_effect: The first request is rejected by authn (error joined, logged, 401). Later requests from the same device are authenticated through the cache.
contracts.failure_mode: DB errors other than the limit error are logged and auth proceeds; the limit error is returned only once per cache period

contracts.action: AnonDBStore constructed inside ProvideAnonymousDeviceService with a device limit
contracts.equivalent_path: The wire provider anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore in pkg/server/wire.go
contracts.before_after: wire.go still lists the provider and binding, but the provider now needs an int64 and has no consumer
contracts.visible_effect: Wire generation fails, so the server does not build

contracts.action: updateDevice treats 0 affected rows as limit reached
contracts.before_after: The MySQL DSN sets clientFoundRows=true, so matched-but-unchanged rows still count as affected

summary: This PR adds an `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` setting: once the limit is reached, new anonymous devices fail authentication and known devices are only updated. Two blockers. First, `pkg/server/wire.go` still registers `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore`, which now needs an `int64` and has no consumer, so wire generation fails. Second, `tagDeviceUI` caches the device key before the DB write and never clears it on error, so a device over the limit is rejected once and then let in for the next 29 minutes, which makes the limit useless. Smaller points: count-then-insert is not atomic; tagging is now synchronous on the auth path even with no limit set; the existing-device update path has no test; the setting is not documented; and the TS field type is inferred as `undefined` while the backend sends a number.
